status: prototype-placeholder | D-023 slice 3 (4 Sep 2026): typed currency - four kinds replace the coin

stations.design_purpose: The first station: assembled bare-handed from gathered wood and placed anywhere. Burns no fuel; it gates kit assembly, not metallurgy.
Placed from a Forge Kit assembled at the workbench. Its processes burn fuel (wood or charcoal), making power the fourth gate from the first hour.

Upgraded in place at a built forge. Consumes most of the mine-order payment plus useful output, so the upgrade feels earned through work rather than passively unlocked. Bog iron (Wave 7 slice 2; the owner, 4 Sep 2026: forge 2 in the first hour was the spike that made you unkillable) is the fen's iron and only the fen drops it - the lurkers most kills, the wisps sometimes - so the second forge, and the tempering and the iron armour behind it, are fetched from the place that is already denser than you: the world steps up a beat before your power does.
Where rough stone is worked into building stone (D-021). Founded from its kit like the bench and the forge; burns no fuel.

recipes.design_purpose: The bench kept alive (Wave 5 item 11): a bundle of eight wedges from three timber, against two from one by hand. The owner (4 Sep 2026) is unsure wedges should be a big thing to craft - 'okay for now' - so the bench makes them cheap rather than the seam making them optional.
The frame the yard's and the forge's kits are built on: jointed at the bench, so the bench stays in the chain for every station the valley founds.
The Ranger's first weapon at the basic forge: a stave and iron tips, as cheap as the mace (the class gear pass, 4 Sep 2026).
Era two's bow: bronze limbs, a tier-three base.
Sewn at the bench from the elk's hide: the Ranger's offhand, and the leather line's first piece.
The first-hour shield: planks and a hide strap at the bench, six armour for anyone.
The Warden's offhand at the basic forge, priced like the mace.
The Kindler's first weapon: a stave shod in iron and charred in the forge's own coals.
The Kindler's offhand: an iron lantern of coals.
The start-with-nothing rung: gather wood by hand, lash a bench together in the field, place it (B, Tab to the kit).

D-021: wood is how you enter the stone age. A wedge set in a seam and driven (E, or a heavy blow) splits stone; each split spends the wedge. Hand-made anywhere, so nobody is ever stuck without a quarry.
The yard is where split stone becomes masonry: timber frames and a fieldstone bed. Its cost is the first thing fieldstone is for.

Two split stones dress into one block of the stone family. Masonry is dearer and slower than timber on purpose (D-021): the first house is wood because that is what the materials can do, and the forge kit's eight stone is the first real masonry ambition.
Assembled at the workbench from all three gathered families, then placed to found the forge; replaces the pre-built forge site.
Slow-burned wood: four times the fuel value per unit, so smiths who plan their burns spend fewer trips hauling logs.
Two ore plus flux wood into one ingot; the forge also burns 2 fuel per smelt, so ore trips and wood trips stay coupled.

The first alloy (D-019): two ores that only surface once the deep wakes, combined at the forge you already have. Bronze is malleable and tough - the building family that works curved forms and the item base that holds a second modifier tier - so era two's new ground leads straight to era two's new work. Old ores never become trash: bronze needs copper forever.
Era three's metal: iron worked again with charcoal at the improved forge. Hard and resilient; old iron never becomes trash because steel needs it forever (D-019).
Silver from the high crags once the ash tide rises: the warding family, and malleable like bronze.

A kind from rare metal (D-023 slice 3): two steel make a Vanguard at the improved forge, so a smith deep in era three can cast the defence kind rather than hunt for it. Steel is era three's alloy; the route never outpaces the hunt before then.
A kind from rare metal and the living: silver and hide make a Marrow. Silver is era three's; hide is the elk's.
A kind from rare metal: two silver make a Quicksilver at the improved forge. Catalysts are never cast: the trial and the families hold them.
The first weapon, craftable at the basic forge: its implicit physical damage is the first felt step above bare hands (D-014 slice 1).
The cold stat-stick needs the improved forge and Blacksmithing 3, so the freeze-shatter build is earned through the same forge ladder as armour.
The fire stat-stick sits on the same rung as the sceptre (improved forge, Blacksmithing 3) and burns one more charcoal: the two casting weapons are a choice, not a ladder.
Cheap third slot with a small resistance implicit; its rolled modifiers (from drops) are where a build gets pulled sideways.
The era-two weapon base: bronze from the deep, so a sceptre that can hold tier three is a sceptre with copper and tin trips behind it (D-019).
The era-two chest base that holds tier-three defence rolls.

catalyst_processes.status: provisional (Proposal C of ADR-0002; D-007 remains open)
catalyst_processes.design_purpose: The catalyst guarantees the domain (fire resistance lands, at tier 2) while the magnitude stays a bounded roll; minimum_roll_fraction raises the roll floor at the required skill so mastery buys consistency, and an existing better roll is never downgraded (preservation)

catalyst_processes.status: D-019: the preservation class of ADR-0002, doing its first real job
catalyst_processes.design_purpose: Moves the worn item's rolled modifiers, whole, onto a base in the pack of the same slot; the old base is spent with the catalyst. This is how a held-back roll is unleashed (an iron sceptre's tier-three cold onto bronze) and how a loved early find is never thrown away. The catalyst is the gate, not the skill: it drops rarely from the stone husks and shriekers of the hills and caves, and from elites' extra passes.

basic_temper.design_purpose: Quenching at a forge that supports basic_temper adds fire resistance at exactly the tier-1 midpoint, so the upgraded forge produces baseline resistance deterministically; the catalyst path is where the roll lives.

fuels.design_purpose: Fuel value per unit when a station process burns fuel. Charcoal concentrates wood four-to-one so refining fuel is worth forge time; the first rung of the power ladder (crafting-and-skills.md four gates).

craft_rolls.design_purpose: Crafted gear rolls modifiers like a drop (owner, 3 Sep 2026: 'they come out plain ... a random generation of modifiers is preferred'). A recipe whose output is an item base makes a rolled item in the pack instead of a stack: keen with keen_chance_at_level_1 plus keen_chance_per_level per Blacksmithing level above one, wrought (rolled first) from wrought_chance_from_level at wrought_chance_per_level per level above that, else plain. The tier is the era's, so era two's forge makes era two's rolls, and the seed is the craft count so a save replays its luck. Infrastructure stays the dependable route: the base is certain, the roll is the excitement.

currency_weighting.design_purpose: A kind added to a gear craft (D-023 slice 3) is consumed and aims the roll: the first modifier is drawn from the kind's family (its items.json tag: offence, defence, life, speed) among what the base allows, and a result that would have been plain is at least aimed_minimum_rarity. The base is still certain, the roll is still the excitement, and now it can be aimed. A family the base cannot hold aims nothing and the kind is still spent: the panel says which families a base allows.

market.design_purpose: The peddler at the spawn clearing prices in kinds now (D-023 slice 3): survival goods for a Marrow or a Quicksilver, steep next to gathering so infrastructure stays the dependable route. The exchange is the reason to come: rate of one kind for one of another among the kinds listed, so a surplus is never dead and a Preserving Transfer is always three kinds away when the husks are unkind. The Ember Catalyst is not for exchange: the trial holds it.

design_purpose_currencies: The purse (D-023 slice 3): the three kinds that stack as numbers rather than pack items. The coin is retired (owner, 4 Sep 2026: 'retire the coin for now'); a coin and a generated town may return later. Catalysts stay pack materials because tempering consumes them from the pack; they are a kind all the same (currency_kinds).

currency_kinds.design_purpose: Works fire through each ingot's purpose: Ember plants a fuse, Edge cuts a cinder seam, Reach sends a travelling spark, Plate heats a retaliation, Ward cauterises afflictions, Haste releases stored burn early, Vigour sheds healing cinders and Frost interrupts with steam. Downstream of Smoulder, it evolves into Steam Plume. Exact identity controls inward Foundry forms; gear crafts still use craft_tag or the currency family.

design_purpose_currency_kinds: D-025: each Kind has a crafting use and an exact Foundry identity. Gear crafts still use craft_tag or the currency family to select their first modifier, and guarantee at least keen. Kinds remain in the four existing families. The pack/purse split and three-for-one exchange are preserved. Frost Catalyst is a pack material dropped by Gloom Crawlers at 7% and available in the exchange; it aims cold crafts and can turn an Ember support into Smoulder. Rare build-defining equipment modifiers remain future work.
